subject: Logging controls & header redaction — post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Logging controls & header redaction — post-call recap

Hi Alicia — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on request/response logging and header/trace-id handling. I kept this intentionally short so we can move to engineering details quickly.

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Only US residency for production logs (no cross-region replication).
- 90-day aggregation retention for audit logs; raw request/response retention limited to 7 days by default unless explicitly requested.
- Headers: need redaction or hashing for sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email, X-Trace-Id) before any long-term storage.
- Trace IDs: remove or replace with non-linkable pseudonyms in any persisted telemetry; transient use for routing is OK inside the runtime if not written to durable logs.
- Proof we can run a short PoC showing sanitized logs without changes to your app instrumentation.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Share a one-page PoC checklist and the minimal log sample schema you requested (attached).
2) Ben (cc'd) to propose two implementation patterns we support for header redaction (runtime-side masking vs. pre-ingest pipeline).
3) Engineering sync next Wed — 45 minutes — to walk through PoC scope and produce a small sample sanitized log export.
4) We will provide SOC2 evidence and our redaction playbook.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20280314.pdf (notes from call).

Would love to confirm the PoC target environment (prod-like vs. staging) and the engineering contact for the sync. If Dan is the right person for technical details, please loop him in.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls & header redaction — post-call recap

Marissa — good summary. A few operational notes from my side before the eng sync: 

- We should offer two paths for the PoC:
  * Runtime masking: Redwood runtime performs header/trace-id redaction prior to any write to persistent logs. Minimal customer changes, low latency impact for short sessions.
  * Ingest-side hook: a lightweight pre-ingest lambda that strips/pseudonymizes headers, useful if the customer wants control outside our runtime.

- For trace IDs, recommend deterministic hashing with a per-customer salt we rotate quarterly (this preserves de-dup semantics without linking back to raw IDs).
- For retention, confirm whether ClearHealth requires deletion notices or just automated TTLs. If they require deletion confirmations, we will need to add an audit step to the PoC.

I'll prepare a two-slide engineering brief and the PoC checklist (I can draft now and Marissa can send). Also recommend we bring Anu from infra to the sync (she's familiar with our KV cache and masking hooks).

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Alicia Vega <alicia@clearhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Sullivan <dan.sullivan@clearhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Logging controls & header redaction — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — confirmed on most of this and appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications/questions from the security team: 

- Residency: production logs must stay within our US tenancy and cannot be replicated to EU or APAC regions. We understand staged/PoC data can be in Redwood staging but would prefer the PoC be run against a US-hosted staging environment.
- Retention: 90 days for aggregated audit logs is desired; however, for raw request/response payloads we want default retention of 7 days and an ability to request expedited deletion for a specific customer PID (we'll provide a list during PoC).
- Headers & Trace-ids: we need a sample sanitized log that demonstrates header redaction and trace-id pseudonymization. Please include a readme that explains what was redacted and why.
- Evidence: Can you provide your latest SOC2 + a short tech note on your redaction process? The security team prefers a short doc rather than full audit until later stages.

I've attached a short sample log schema our team uses (sample-log-schema.xlsx) — it includes the fields we'd like to see mapped. Dan will be our primary eng contact; looping him in now.

Can we target the engineering sync for next Wed at 10am PT? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and provide the staging credentials needed for the PoC.

Best,
Alicia Vega
Director, Security & Privacy
ClearHealth Solutions
alicia@clearhealth.com

Alicia / Dan — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround and the schema. Wed 10am PT works on our side; please send the invite and staging details when ready.

Attached is the PoC checklist we suggested (poc-checklist.md). High-level plan:
- Day 0: share staging credentials + sample PID list.
- Day 1–2: Redwood runs a sanitized export against staging and produces a readme describing redaction steps.
- Day 3: Joint review of sanitized sample and run-through of retention/deletion workflow.

Action items we are taking before the call:
- Ben: two-page eng brief + proposed pseudonymization hash design and config options.
- Neha: SOC2 cover note and redaction playbook (we'll paste the short version into the drive link).
- Marissa: coordinate invite and confirm PoC success criteria (I will add a short acceptance criteria table to the checklist).

If anything changes on your side, flag it in reply-all and we will adjust. Looking forward to the sync.

Thanks —
